sources.title: poteto/brainmaxxing: persistent memory for Claude Code
How I Use Cursor (X article, linked from flaviocopes.com/pstack)
Trust First, Then Parallel (secondary summary of her talk)

philosophy: Go deep before going fast: make one agent trustworthy on a whole problem (write less, better, verified code), then parallelise. Turn each correction into structure such as lint rules, types or skills, not more prose.
process: First: /pstack:setup-pstack to pick a reasoning budget and the model for each role (re-run it when pstack's defaults change; an older rule keeps pinning the old defaults)
Start rigorous work with /pstack:poteto-mode, which matches the task to a playbook (bug fix, feature, refactor, perf, investigation...) and copies its steps into a todo list
Understand first: /how and /why for code walkthroughs and design rationale
Design before code: /architect sketches types, signatures and modules
Build, then clean: /unslop for prose, /no-comments (Comment Sicko subagent) for code
Verify with evidence: a project-local verification skill (/create-verification-skill) plus adversarial multi-model review (/interrogate)

Encode lessons (/reflect captures the recipe as a skill edit; /correct turns repeated mistakes into types, lint, CI or tests). Once one agent's output can be trusted, parallelise (/swarm, /arena, autopilot playbooks)
tools: lint rules / type checker / CI as guardrails

sources.title: Embracing the parallel coding agent lifestyle
Claude Skills are awesome, maybe a bigger deal than MCP
Introducing Showboat and Rodney, so agents can demo what they've built

philosophy: Agentic engineering means professionals amplifying their expertise with agents. Code is cheap now, so spend effort on tests, proof that the code works, and safe sandboxes. Prefer CLI tools and skills over MCP.
process: Open each session with 'First run the tests' (for example uv run pytest) so the agent knows the suite exists
Implement with 'Use red/green TDD'
Have the agent prove the feature by hand-testing it and recording a demo (showboat, with rodney for browser screenshots)
Understand unfamiliar code through linear walkthroughs and interactive explanations
Run agents in parallel for research, scouting attempts, small maintenance and carefully specified tasks, each in a fresh checkout

Prefer YOLO mode in a sandbox or on someone else's computer (Docker, Codespaces, Codex Cloud, Claude Code for web) with test/staging credentials and a tight budget; he admits he also runs it locally when he is confident no malicious instructions can reach the context

name: Geoffrey Huntley
role: Engineer and writer who created the 'Ralph Wiggum' agent loop technique.

sources.title: The Ralph Playbook (Clayton Farr; fork at ghuntley/how-to-ralph-wiggum)

philosophy: Software is built as a loop, not brick by brick: a bash while-loop that feeds the same prompt to a fresh agent context, one task per iteration, with tests and type checks as backpressure. Watch the loop and tune the prompt whenever it fails.
process: Talk through the idea and write one spec per topic in specs/*.md
Planning prompt: have Ralph study the specs and the source and create or update a prioritised @fix_plan.md, then switch from planning to building mode
Building loop: while :; do cat PROMPT.md | <agent> ; done, picking the single most important item per iteration
Main context acts as scheduler; subagents search and summarise (many in parallel) but only one runs build/test
Backpressure: tests, type checkers and static analysis; no placeholders; commit and tag when green
Watch the stream; when it misbehaves, tune the prompt (add a 'sign') and let Ralph keep @AGENT.md up to date, or git reset --hard and start the loop again
Prefer greenfield projects
tools: type checkers / static analysers (e.g. Pyrefly, Dialyzer)
